heroHeadline: Trump and Rodríguez Hold First-Ever Meeting as Venezuela Pledges Elections — Without a Date
heroSubtitle: President Trump and interim President Delcy Rodríguez met face-to-face for the first time on September 23 at the UN General Assembly, discussing energy, mining, security and debt restructuring in what Rodríguez called a "historic" encounter; the next day she told the Assembly "elections will be held in Venezuela" while declining to set a date, drawing criticism that Washington has traded election demands for oil and investment access. The same week, opposition leader María Corina Machado made her fifth through seventh failed attempts to re-enter Venezuela by sea and air as authorities blocked her at every route, while a second round of US-backed government-opposition talks concluded September 26 with an agreement to review Supreme Tribunal of Justice candidate selection — the first concrete judicial-reform step since the January capture of Maduro. Foro Penal counted 344 political prisoners still detained as of September 14, down from 391 in late August, and Chevron signed a new $7B+ joint-venture deal on September 2 targeting a doubling of its Venezuelan output, even as monthly inflation slowed to an 18-month low of 8.9% in August against a bolívar that has now passed 857 to the dollar.
